tldr: The pointwise causal effect \(\tau(z_0)\) is identified despite a noisy confounding control, but clean observation of the modifier does not recover ordinary regression resolution. On the specified full class with unknown positive smooth density and jointly Hölder-\(1/10\) confounding functions, the exact original-record minimax absolute-risk rate is \(n^{-2/53}\). An explicit total inverse-pair estimator attains it, and class-legal crossed-frame mixtures give a matching lower bound for all measurable original-record procedures. The contrast-oracle and randomized-subclass benchmarks have rate \(n^{-1/3}\). The separation measures the cost of noisy adjustment for a heterogeneous effect indexed by an accurately observed modifier.
gap: Published CATE rate theory observes the adjustment covariates, while circular inverse-functional theory does not impose a binary causal likelihood or homogeneous effects across the noisy coordinate. Their conjunction does not determine the supplied split-coordinate experiment.
